Talking About Uncertain Past Events
You can use modal verbs to talk about uncertain events in the past.

You use these structures to talk about the past. Each one has slightly different meaning, but they all imply uncertainty and speculation.

  • must have + past participle
    • You use this structure to speculate about past events taking into account that we are pretty sure what happened.

  • might / might not have + past participle and may / may not have + past participle
    • You use these structures to speculate about something that happened in the past but we are not sure about it.

  • could / couldn't have + past participle
    • You use this to express that something was possible or you had the skill to do it but you did not do it.

  • can't have + past participle
    • You use this structure to express certainty that something did not happen in the past.

You : Where was Dave last night?
Jason:
Something must have come up.
He might have had to work.
He could have left work late.
He may have gone to the wrong place.
He can't have forgotten.
The staff may be busy and might have forgotten about the playlist.
They may have felt a younger sound would make that place seem more energetic.
That kind of music might have worked in another locale.
They could have thought that's the style nowadays.
People can't have enjoyed themselves in there, could they?
Cause and Effect: So + clause
So introduces a clause that expresses an effect (result) of the cause expressed in the main clause.

For example:

He saw an old lady struggling with her bags, so he helped her.
You use a comma to separate the so clause from the main clause.
I heard it had amazing desserts, so I thought we should try it.
I have finished my diet last week, so now I can have some cheese cake.
I ate only a salad for dinner, so I'm going to have the chocolate cake.
It's too loud, so I can't hear what you are saying.
It's just too loud in here, so we are going to have to leave.
The server didn't help, for she knew she could do nothing.
